checks: The saved source string is hashed before parsing/enabling controls; strict envelope/state keys and source-bound ordinal criterion keys preserve duplicate/missing source IDs as distinct entries.

Read-only numeric labels are rendered and escaped by Python before browser JSON parsing; local state only uses exact string identity/ordinal keys, status strings and literal notes. No grades or rating selection are inferred.

Save captures and validates live controls, clones the document and embeds the exact source string plus detached local state. Reopening starts hidden/disabled and restores values only after schema/digest/binding admission.

Notes embedded in JSON escape markup delimiters and line separators. Display uses textContent; the fixed JS/CSS remain hash-authorized under the cloned CSP. Literal source names/metadata are escaped by the single-pass Python renderer.

Failed preparation does not clear controls or mutate the original file. Temporary anchors/URLs are cleaned; wording accurately asks the user to confirm the requested download rather than claiming durable save.

Print state is separate from editable controls. Literal notes are reflected into pre-wrap print elements; CSS exposes supplied details/ratings without choosing a score, and labels retain original large numeric metadata.
Read-only same-origin HTTP(S) source links are explicit; no browser fetch, autosave or storage path appears in this code.
limitations: Source review only: no browser launch, suite rerun, provider request or source edit by this reviewer. Actual saved-copy reopen/download/CSP/print behavior remains the author browser receiver responsibility.

The SHA256 is an embedded-source corruption check, not a signature or authentication of the complete HTML. JavaScript verifies criterion key/order consistency; it does not cryptographically revalidate every pre-rendered card text against the source blob. No whole-file tamperproof claim is made.
Current modern-browser Unicode admission uses String.isWellFormed when available; this review does not establish equivalent lone-surrogate behavior on older browsers lacking that method.
Input and publication reuse remains covered by the existing native/independent receiving, not newly executed here. No Actions-triggering publication performed.
